Sparse query-based 3D detectors commonly encode heterogeneous semantic, geo-
metric, and motion information into unified latent queries, including when explicit 3D
anchors are used. We introduce ExQuery, an explicit structured query framework for
temporal 3D object detection. Each decoded query is organized into a shared semantic-
context slice and physical-state-specific slices for center, dimensions, orientation, and
velocity. This structure is preserved from prior encoding to branch-specific regression
and is reused to reconstruct temporal queries: predicted physical states are transformed
by ego motion, classification scores form soft semantic priors, and the reconstructed
query is fused with the stored latent instance feature through gated affine modulation.
Experiments on the nuScenes benchmark show that our method achieves competitive

evidence.excerpt:
Table 1 compares our method with representative camera-based 3D object detectors on the
nuScenes validation set. With the ResNet-50 image backbone and an input resolution of
256×704, our method achieves 0.459 mAP and 0.561 NDS. Compared with StreamPETR,
our method improves mAP from 0.450 to 0.459 and NDS from 0.550 to 0.561. With the ex-
plicit propagated priors, it also reduces several box-quality errors, including mATE, mASE,
mAOE, and mA VE, indicating that the proposed method benefits detection accuracy.
RepDETR3D and ExQuery use the same ResNet-50 backbone, FPN neck, 256×704 in-
put resolution, and runtime settings. Table 2 reports the computational overhead of ExQuery
under this matched setup: 2.88M parameters, 2.57 GFLOPs, and 11.57 MB of measured
memory, with latency increasing from 14.88 to 18.48 ms.

we zero out one slice at a time before the prediction heads and measure the metric difference
∆m=m intervention −m normal. For NDS and mAP, negative values indicate degraded detection
performance, while for mATE, mASE, mAOE, and mA VE, positive values indicate increased
error. Since the shared slice is designed as a common semantic-context pathway rather than
a physical-state-specific slice, zeroing the shared slice causes large degradation across all
metrics, so we focus this analysis on the physical slices.

Structured query slice intervention.To analyze the functional role of each physical slice,
we zero out one slice at a time before the prediction heads and measure the metric difference
∆m=m intervention −m normal. For NDS and mAP, negative values indicate degraded detection
performance, while for mATE, mASE, mAOE, and mA VE, positive values indicate increased
error. Since the shared slice is designed as a common semantic-context pathway rather than
a physical-state-specific slice, zeroing the shared slice causes large degradation across all
metrics, so we focus this analysis on the physical slices.

evidence.excerpt:
We presented ExQuery, which preserves a shared/physical channel organization in 3D object
queries from explicit prior encoding to temporal reconstruction and branch-specific regres-
sion. Experiments show competitive detection performance, while the ablations support the
complementary roles of structured queries, explicit priors, and gated fusion.
Despite these encouraging results, several directions remain open for further exploration.
In our current design, the shared semantic-context slice is intentionally used by all prediction
branches, allowing physical prediction to benefit from contextual cues. The added query en-
coders and fusion module also introduce a measurable latency cost. A deeper understanding
of what information is involved in the query, and how to further encourage attribute-specific
specialization without losing useful contextual interaction, remains an important

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The model is optimized against ground-truth annotations and evaluated with fixed benchmark metrics on a separate validation split; no learned or automated judge is reused across optimization and final assessment.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Fixed official nuScenes validation metrics (mAP, NDS, and true-positive error metrics) on the held-out validation split.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training loss computed against ground-truth nuScenes 3D annotations, including bounding box regression, classification, and denoising objectives.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The reported experimental numbers substantiate the scoped claims, demonstrating competitive detection performance (0.561 NDS and 0.459 mAP on nuScenes val) and confirming the functional specialization of the sliced physical representations via ablation and intervention experiments.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is conducted on the standard nuScenes 3D detection benchmark against established baselines (StreamPETR, Sparse4D, BEVNeXt) reporting official metrics including NDS, mAP, and TP errors. Detailed ablation studies isolate the contributions of channel slicing, explicit prior propagation, fusion variants, latency/memory footprint, and feature-slice zeroing interventions.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The model is evaluated using fixed standard benchmark metrics on an independent validation set, with no automated or learned judge reused across optimization and final assessment.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark evaluation metrics (mAP, NDS, and TP error metrics) evaluated on the nuScenes validation split.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training loss (bounding box regression, classification, and denoising objectives) computed against ground-truth nuScenes 3D annotations.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge the computational and latency overhead introduced by the additional encoders and modulation modules, the reliance on the shared slice for contextual reasoning, and the need for deeper attribute disentanglement.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the channel partitioning into shared and attribute slices (center, dimension, orientation, velocity), complex-valued positional encodings for angles, ego-motion transformation of physical priors, soft semantic prior construction, and mutual gated affine modulation with stored implicit instance queries.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-formulated technical contribution with clear motivation, comprehensive mathematical descriptions, solid empirical validation on standard benchmarks, and insightful ablation studies.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces ExQuery, a camera-based temporal 3D object detection framework that structures object queries into shared semantic-context and physical-state-specific slices, maintaining this attribute alignment through prior encoding, branch-specific regression, and ego-motion temporal propagation with mutual gated affine modulation.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-formulated technical contribution with clear motivation, comprehensive mathematical descriptions, solid empirical validation on standard benchmarks, and insightful ablation studies.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge the computational and latency overhead introduced by the additional encoders and modulation modules, the reliance on the shared slice for contextual reasoning, and the need for deeper attribute disentanglement.
